Cognitive Flexibility Lens

**Overview**

Cognitive flexibility is the capacity to switch tasks, adapt strategies and reframe problems.  It underpins adaptability in dynamic environments.  This lens highlights each PI profile’s preferred adaptation style (primary), supporting strategy (secondary) and stress pattern when flexibility is strained.

**Crosswalk by PI Profile**

| PI Profile | Primary flexibility style | Secondary strategy | Stress pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Analyzer** | Rule‑based switching | Scenario reframe | Slow to pivot |
| **Controller** | Structured adaptation | Contingency switching | Resists novel paths |
| **Specialist** | Contextual tweak | Method substitution | Sticks to known tools |
| **Strategist** | High flexibility | Multi‑scenario thinking | Overcomplicates pivots |
| **Venturer** | Rapid pivoting | Opportunistic shifts | Chaotic switching |
| **Altruist** | Relational adaptation | Role shifting | Over‑accommodates changes |
| **Captain** | Directive pivot | Fast course correction | Forces change without buy‑in |
| **Collaborator** | Consensus pivot | Group recalibration | Delays to preserve harmony |
| **Maverick** | Creative switching | Radical reframing | Disrupts continuity |
| **Persuader** | Socially adaptive | Message reframing | Chases trends and loses depth |
| **Promoter** | Energetic pivot | Rapid rebranding | Surface‑level shifts only |
| **Adapter** | Situational switching | Role blending | Over‑adjusts identity |
| **Craftsman** | Methodical tweak | Process refinement | Slow to accept new methods |
| **Guardian** | Cautious shift | Protocol adaptation | Blocks change until proven |
| **Operator** | Operational pivot | Workflow reroute | Rigid under ambiguity |
| **Individualist** | Conceptual pivot | Personal reframing | Withdraws when forced |
| **Scholar** | Analytic switching | Theory rework | Over‑tests alternatives |

**Practical recommendations**

* Build bridging mechanisms: Pair high‑flexibility individuals (Venturer, Maverick) with process‑oriented colleagues (Guardian, Craftsman) to balance speed and control.
* Encourage consensus‑oriented profiles (Collaborator, Altruist) to voice concerns early to avoid delayed pivots.  Use structured decision checkpoints to maintain momentum.
* Provide templates for rule‑based switchers (Analyzer, Controller) to help them adapt more quickly when the context changes.  Highlight boundary conditions where rules may no longer apply.
* Recognise that creative pivots (Maverick, Individualist) can generate disruptive innovation but may destabilise teams.  Establish clear communication channels to align the group.
